title: Nuclear depletion of RNA binding protein ELAVL3 (HuC) in sporadic and familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
authors: Sandra Diaz-Garcia; Vivian I. Ko; Sonia Vazquez-Sanchez; Ruth Chia; Olubankole Aladesuyi Arogundade; Maria J Rodriguez; Don Cleveland; Bryan J. Traynor; John Ravits
one_liner_zh: 该文研究ALS中RNA结合蛋白ELAVL3的核耗竭与病理机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a progressive fatal neurodegenerative disease caused by loss of motor neurons and characterized neuropathologically in almost all cases by nuclear depletion and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43, a nuclear RNA binding protein (RBP). We identified ELAVL3 as one of the most downregulated genes in our transcriptome profiles of laser captured microdissection of motor neurons from sporadic ALS nervous systems and the top dysregulated RBPs. Neuropathological characterizations showed ELAVL3 nuclear depletion in a great percentage of remnant motor neurons, sometimes accompanied by cytoplasmic accumulations. These abnormalities were common in sporadic cases with and without intermediate expansions in ATXN2 and familial cases carrying mutations in C9orf72 and SOD1. Depletion of ELAVL3 occurred at both the RNA and protein levels and a short protein isoform was identified but it is not related to a TDP-43-dependent cryptic exon in intron 3. Strikingly, ELAVL3 abnormalities were more frequent than TDP-43 abnormalities and occurred in motor neurons still with normal nuclear TDP-43 present, but all neurons with abnormal TDP-43 also had abnormal ELAVL3. In a neuron-like cell culture model using SH-SY5Y cells, ELAVL3 mislocalization occurred weeks before TDP-43 abnormalities were seen. We interrogated genetic databases but did not identify association of ELAVL3 genetic structure associated with ALS. Taken together, these findings suggest that ELAVL3 is an important RBP in ALS pathogenesis acquired early and the neuropathological data suggest it is involved by loss of function rather than cytoplasmic toxicity.
abstract_zh: 肌萎缩侧索硬化是一种进行性致命的神经退行性疾病，由运动神经元丧失引起，并在几乎所有病例中，其神经病理学特征表现为核内TDP-43（一种核RNA结合蛋白 (RNA binding protein, RBP)）的耗竭和胞质聚集。我们在散发性ALS神经系统运动神经元的激光捕获显微切割转录组谱中，将ELAVL3鉴定为下调最显著的基因之一，同时也是失调最显著的RBP之一。神经病理学特征显示，在大部分残留运动神经元中，ELAVL3核内耗竭，有时伴有胞质积聚。这些异常在携带或不携带ATXN2中间长度扩展的散发病例以及携带C9orf72和SOD1突变的家族性病例中均常见。ELAVL3的耗竭发生在RNA和蛋白质两个水平，并鉴定出一种短蛋白亚型，但其与TDP-43依赖的内含子3中的隐蔽外显子无关。显著的是，ELAVL3异常比TDP-43异常更频繁，且发生在核内TDP-43仍正常的运动神经元中，但所有具有异常TDP-43的神经元也表现出异常的ELAVL3。在使用SH-SY5Y细胞的神经元样细胞培养模型中，ELAVL3的错误定位在TDP-43异常出现前数周即已发生。我们查询了遗传数据库，但未发现ELAVL3遗传结构与ALS的关联。综合来看，这些发现表明ELAVL3是ALS发病过程中早期获得的重要RBP，且神经病理学数据提示其通过功能丧失而非胞质毒性参与发病。
